sentences.text: The only known specimen of Polonosuchus is a fragmentary holotype, which serves as the single physical basis for the species description.
This fossil preserves various skull bones including the maxillae, premaxillae, nasals, and several jaw and palate elements.
The specimen includes the first three neck vertebrae, nine tail vertebrae, some tail scutes, and fragments of neck ribs.
At least eleven tooth sockets were present in the maxillae, though the total number is uncertain due to damage.
The prefrontal bones were large triangular plates that overhung the eye sockets and had rough lateral surfaces.
The squamosal bone possessed five distinct projections.
The front part of the lower jaw is preserved, showing up to the first eight teeth.
Only the centrum of the atlas vertebra is preserved, featuring a crescent shape and a rounded front surface.
The tail vertebrae had prominent facets for haemal arches and tall, plate-like neural spines.
Five dermal scutes found near the tail vertebrae likely belonged to the tail region.
The two largest scutes were rectangular with articulatory processes, suggesting they overlapped and linked together.
Polonosuchus differs from Teratosaurus in having a rostromedial foramen on the medial maxilla surface and replacement tooth foramina arranged in a straight line rather than a groove.
Polonosuchus had a larger first tooth socket, smaller overall maxillae measuring 165 mm versus 245 mm, and a unique ridge between the palatal process and tooth sockets not found in Teratosaurus.
Evidence of replacement teeth suggests Polonosuchus was likely a polyphyodont, continuously replacing its teeth throughout life.
The genus Polonosuchus was formally described by Brusatte and colleagues in 2009.
The species was originally described in 2005 by Tomasz Sulej under the name Teratosaurus silesiacus.
Polonosuchus was a predator characterized by a large head containing long, sharp teeth.
Its legs were positioned almost directly beneath its body, suggesting it was a fast and powerful runner.
Polonosuchus shared a similar appearance and the ecological niche of an apex predator with the North American genus Postosuchus.
Polonosuchus is classified as a distinct genus within the Rauisuchia.
Polonosuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
Polonosuchus is classified in the order Rauisuchia.
Polonosuchus falls within the unranked group Crurotarsi.
Polonosuchus lived during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic in Poland.
Polonosuchus lived between 233.6 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
It is debated whether Polonosuchus is distinct enough from Teratosaurus suevicus, as it is still considered closely related to that species.
